AppEvent.description: What the app sends the UI on the channel the UI registers at boot (`app_events`).

oneOf.description:
The window's close button, Alt+F4 or `WM_CLOSE`: the close is held until the UI answers
with `app_quit` (after the save prompt), or not at all when the user cancels.

BandLossUi.description: A band's particle loss: lost by meshing problems plus lost by infinite loops, over its total.

pct.description: The loss in percent, two decimals, rounded half up in integers ([`loss_pct`]).

BandSet.description:
The frequency bands every per-band value in the project is given on.

`frequencies_hz` holds nominal centre frequencies of `kind`, strictly ascending. The solvers
sort `freq_enum` and map every per-band array by sorted position, so ascending order here is
the order of every per-band array in the project.

send_failures.description: Batches the sink refused (the webview went away, for example).

CheckCounts.description: The check's counts that the UI shows.

boundary_open_edges.description: Open edges on the outer shell, after analysis.

open_edges.description: Census edges used once (by index, before analysis).

CheckReasonOut.description: One reason the check refused the geometry.

count.description: How many findings, as the message counts them.

CheckSummary.description: The model check, for the Geometry panel and the view's highlight.

bbox_min.description: The bounding box of the vertices the faces use.

enclosed_volume_m3.description:
The volume the faces enclose; `None` when the check refuses the model, whose "volume" is
not a number anyone should read (a refused model encloses no volume, M10 MINOR B-18).

highlight_faces.description: Every face any reason names, ascending, unique.

reasons.description: In the core's reason order; empty exactly when the verdict is ok.

CmdError.description: An error for the UI: a stable reason code and a message for people.

Directivity.description:
Source directivity: `source@directivite`, the solver's `SOURCE_TYPE`
(`lib_interface/coreTypes.h:96-104`). See [`Directivity::solver_code`].

In JSON: `{"kind": "omni"}`, `{"kind": "unidirectional", "direction": [x, y, z]}`, ...
Extra keys are refused for every kind. (serde's derive alone would read
`{"kind": "omni", "file": "balloon.txt"}` as omni and drop the file, so the reader is written
by hand.)

oneOf.description: Code 0.
Code 1: emits along `direction` (`@u`, `@v`, `@w`, normalised by the solver).

direction.description: [x, y, z] in metres, Z up

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

oneOf.description: Code 2: emits in the XY plane.
Code 3: emits in the YZ plane.
Code 4: emits in the XZ plane.

Code 5: a directivity balloon file (`@directivity_file`), aimed along `direction`.
`file` is relative to the project file. A missing file makes the source emit nothing,
with exit code 0 (contract survey, `run_dirmiss`), so it is checked before launch.

direction.description: [x, y, z] in metres, Z up

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

EditOutcome.description: The result of `edit_apply`, the checked apply (PLAN.md 1.8).

applied.description: False when the validator refused the edit: the project and its history are unchanged.

refusals.description: The new errors the edit would have introduced.

EntityRef.description:
A named entity of the project. In JSON: `{"kind": "material", "id": "<uuid>"}`; any other
key is refused.

FloatProbe.description: What each reader made of a JSON array of numbers: the bits as `0x` + 16 hex digits.

disagreements.description: How many values the two readers disagree on.

exact_bits.description: Read with the core's exact reader, as every schema value from the UI is.

serde_json_bits.description: Read with `serde_json::from_str`, as a command argument typed `f64` would be.

GroupStats.description: A surface group's geometry facts, and whether it has a real material.

assigned.description:
False when its effective material under the active variant is the placeholder
([`is_placeholder`]).

LibraryMaterial.description: One of upstream's reference materials, as the library adds it (`library_material`).

absorption.description: The `f32`-widened absorption, the same in every band, as a `.proj` import makes it.

LineClass.description: The Console's classes (docs/design/README.md: FAIL, INFO and OK; WARN for the amber lines).

unclassified.description: Of the WARN lines, those no pattern matched.

LineSource.description:
Where a streamed line came from: the solver (classified by the core) or TetGen while the run
meshes (INFO).

LossUi.description: SPPS's particle loss, as the verdict holds it against the limit: per band.

worst_pct.description: The largest band's `pct` (the first such band on a tie).

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

double_sided.description: `@side_material`: the material acts on both sides of a face.

reflection_law.description: `bfreq@loi`, one law for every band or one per band.

scattering.description:
Scattering coefficient per band, 0 to 1: the share of reflections that are diffuse
(`bfreq@diffusion`).

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

solver_id.description:
A pinned solver id (`type_surface@id`, the `.cbin` face `idMat`). `None` lets export
assign one. Importers set it so that a project imported from a solver mesh exports the
same ids and still matches that mesh. At most [`SOLVER_INT_MAX`]: the solver reads
`@id` with `atoi`.

transmission_loss_db.description:
Transmission loss per band in dB (`bfreq@affaiblissement`, tau = 10^(-R/10)). `None`
means no transmission in any band; a `None` band does not transmit. Either way the
attribute is left out of that band, which is how the solver knows
(`base_core_configuration.cpp:210-219`), as upstream's GUI leaves it out of a band whose
`transmission` switch is off (`e_data_row_materiau.h:98-106`): tutorial 3's
`Open_door` transmits from 250 Hz to 4 kHz but not at 125 Hz.

anyOf.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

background_noise.description: Background noise, `bfreq@db` per band. `None` writes none.

name.description: `@lbl` and `@name`. SPPS makes it a folder name and TCR a file name.

orientation.description: `@u`, `@v`, `@w`, normalised by the solver; must not be zero.

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

position.description: `@x`, `@y`, `@z`; must lie inside the meshed volume.

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

solver_id.description:
A pinned solver id (`recepteur_ponctuel@id`). `None` lets export assign one
(`config_xml`, "Solver ids"). A `.proj` import pins upstream's element id (its `wxid`,
`docs/m5-m6-design.md`, decision 13), so an imported project writes upstream's ids. At
most [`SOLVER_INT_MAX`], and unique among point receivers.

Prepared.description: A prepared buffer: take it with `token`; `checksum` is [`checksum`] of its bytes.

ProjectInfo.description: What the chrome shows about the open project: names and counts, never an acoustic value.

dirty.description: Changed since it was last saved or opened, or never saved.

geometry_rev.description: Changes whenever the geometry can have changed; the UI refetches the mesh on a change.

groups_assigned.description:
Surface groups whose effective material is not the import placeholder
(`scene::is_placeholder`).

ReasonUi.description: A reason with its core code and its UI code (row 22 (3): both are shown).

ReflectionLaw.description:
How a surface reflects the diffuse part of the energy: `type_surface/bfreq@loi`, the solver's
`REFLECTION_LAW` (`lib_interface/coreTypes.h:83-92`). The discriminant is the solver code.

SPPS draws a diffuse reflection with probability equal to the scattering coefficient
(`spps/CalculationCore.cpp:318`), so the law has no effect at scattering 0.
[`ReflectionLaw::SemiDiffuse`] has no case in SPPS's `ReflectionLaws::SolveReflection`
(`spps/tools/dotreflection.h:23-45`) and falls to its default, a specular reflection.

oneOf.description: Uniform, `w1` in upstream's comments.

anyOf.description: The same law in every band.
One law per band; its length is the band count (`Project::check_integrity`).

ReflectionLaws.description:
A material's reflection law: one law for every band, or one per band. The solvers read it per
band (`type_surface/bfreq@loi`, `base_core_configuration.cpp:210-219`), and upstream's GUI
keeps one per band (the `loi` list of each row, `e_data_row_materiau.h:218`): tutorial 3's
material 100 is Lambert in the six octave bands and specular in the others.

In JSON: one law, `"lambert"`, or one per band in the band set's order,
`["specular", "lambert", ...]`. [`ReflectionLaws::from_bands`] gives the single spelling
whenever every band has the same law.

ResultsState.description: Whether a run's results verify (`results::load`), never a value from them.

seq.description: 0, 1, 2, ... per run, so the UI can prove it lost nothing and kept the order.

last.description: The producer has finished; no batch follows.

RunLineClass.description: The core's line classes (`docs/solver-contract.md` Part B), as the Console labels them.

RunRow.description: One row of the Runs tab: every field is read from the run's `run.json`, formatted here.

elapsed_s.description: The solver's wall time in seconds, one decimal ([`elapsed_s`]).

exe.description: The solver executable and its sha256.

loss.description: SPPS with its statistics table read.

manifest_error.description: `run.json` is there but does not read.

number.description: 1, 2, ... by start time among this project's runs.

run.description: The folder's name: the row's key.

solvers.description:
The executables checked against the verified build before the run; `None` for a CLI run
or one written before M11.

stage.description: The stage the run ended in.

variant.description: The variant written (its id); `None` for the project's own materials.

RunStarted.description: What `run_start` answers at once; the run itself reports through the stream.

variant.description: The active variant's id, `None` for the project's own materials.

RunStatusUi.description: A run as the Runs tab lists it.

oneOf.description: The active run, whose `run.json` is not written yet.

A run folder with no `run.json` that is not the active run: the app died mid-run
(Stop-Process, a crash). Listed, never dropped and never guessed.

last.description: The run thread has finished; no batch follows.

RunStreamEvent.description:
One event of a run, in order. `seq` is 0, 1, 2, ... per run, so the UI can prove it lost
nothing.

oneOf.description: The run folder exists (the core's `RunEvent::Started`). Always the first event.

run.description: The folder's name: the run's key everywhere in the UI.

oneOf.description: A stage begins: solvers, geometry, validate, mesh, export, pre_launch or solve.
A classified solver line, or a TetGen line (`source: mesh`, INFO).

rule.description: The contract's row id (`spps_end_of_calculation`, ...); empty for a mesh line.

solver_seq.description: The core's arrival index of a solver line (`Classified::seq`).

text.description: Exactly as the program printed it.

oneOf.description: `run.json` is written. `row` is what `runs_list` lists for it.

No run folder with its `run.json` could be made (the core's `RunError`), or the run
thread panicked: `RUN_PROJECT`, `RUN_IO` or `RUN_PANIC`.

RunsView.description: The Runs tab: every run of the open project under its runs root.

other_projects.description: Run folders of other projects under the same root: counted, not listed.

SceneState.description: The state of the open project as the M10 UI shows it. Returned by every M10 command.

check.description: The model check of the current geometry; `None` when the project has no faces.

groups.description: One per surface group, in project order.

issues.description: The validator's issues on the current project, with their UI codes.

lines.description: Console lines produced since the last state was returned.

run_blockers.description:
Why Run is disabled by the project itself, as UI codes; empty when the project may run.
The UI adds the app's own blockers beside them: `SOLVER_NOT_FOUND` and
`SOLVER_UNVERIFIED` (`solvers_status`) and `RUN_ACTIVE` (the run slot).

view.description: The project without its mesh; the mesh travels as bytes (`scene_mesh`).

SolverCheck.description: One executable checked against the manifest.

code_sha256.description: The file's code sha256 (link times zeroed), or why it has none.

SolversStatus.description: The four executables a run needs, each checked against the verified build.

blockers.description: `SOLVER_NOT_FOUND` and/or `SOLVER_UNVERIFIED`; empty when all four are the verified build.

enabled.description: A disabled source is left out of config.xml.

group.description:
The source group it sits in, as upstream's GUI groups sources (a source list's element of
type 15, `e_scene_sources.h:73-87`): the groups' names from the outermost, joined by
` / `. `None` at the top level, as for every source made here. It reaches no solver:
upstream writes a group's sources in its place. Source names need be unique only within
one group (`name_duplicate`), unless per-source output makes them folder names.

position.description:
`@x`, `@y`, `@z`. Must lie strictly inside the meshed volume: SPPS crashes on a source
outside it (contract survey, `run_srcout`).

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

power.description: Sound power, dB re 1 pW (`bfreq@db` per band, from [`Spectrum::band_levels_db`]).

solver_id.description:
A pinned element id: upstream's `source@id` for a source imported from a `.proj` (its
`wxid`, `docs/m5-m6-design.md`, decision 13). `None` for a source made here. The solvers
number sources by position and never read `source@id`
(`base_core_configuration.cpp:153`); `config.xml` carries it when pinned, as upstream's
GUI writes it, so that an imported project keeps upstream's ids. At most
[`SOLVER_INT_MAX`], and unique among sources.

Spectrum.description:
A level spectrum: a global level spread over the project's bands by a shape.

Used for source sound power (dB re 1 pW) and receiver background noise.

global_db.description: The energetic sum over the project's bands, in dB.

SpectrumShape.description:
The shape of a level spectrum across the project's bands.

In JSON: `{"kind": "pink"}`, `{"kind": "white"}` or `{"kind": "custom", "relative_db": [...]}`.
Extra keys are refused for every kind: serde's derive alone would read
`{"kind": "pink", "relative_db": [...]}` as pink and drop the levels, so the reader is written
by hand.

oneOf.description: Equal power in every band.

Power proportional to bandwidth: +1 dB per third-octave band and +3 dB per octave band,
exactly (base-10 bands). This is I-Simpa's "White noise": tutorial 1's source, 80 dB
over 50 Hz to 20 kHz in thirds, reads 60.1404190063477 dB at 1 kHz, and this shape gives
60.14042 dB.
Relative levels in dB, one per band. Only the differences matter.

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

e2e.description: Started with `--e2e`: the UI installs its test hooks.

pid.description: This process's id: the M11 gate sends `WM_CLOSE` to its window and stops it by it.

Stream.description: Where a line came from. Lines are classified by content, never by stream (laydown, Traps).

SurfaceGroup.description: A named set of faces sharing one material: the unit materials are assigned to.

material.description: The base project's material; a [`Variant`] may override it.

solver_id.description:
A pinned solver id (`recepteur_surfacique@id` or `recepteur_surfacique_coupe@id`, and a
scene receiver's `.cbin` `idRs`). `None` lets export assign one (`config_xml`, "Solver
ids"). A `.proj` import pins upstream's element id (decision 13). At most
[`SOLVER_INT_MAX`], and unique among surface receivers and cutting planes.

oneOf.description:
On the model: every face of these surface groups carries this receiver's id as its `.cbin`
`idRs`. A face has one `idRs`, so a group belongs to at most one scene receiver.

A rectangle through corners `a`, `b`, `c` (`@ax`..`@cz`), cut into
`ceil(|bc| / resolution) x ceil(|ba| / resolution)` cells (`@resolution`, metres).

a.description: [x, y, z] in metres, Z up

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

b.description: [x, y, z] in metres, Z up

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

c.description: [x, y, z] in metres, Z up

items.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

resolution_m.description: A float. Finite values are numbers; non-finite values are strings.

UiIssue.description: A validator issue as the UI shows it: the UI code and the core rule, both.

entity.description: The entity the pointer names, resolved in the issue's own project.

field.description:
The pointer after the entity, e.g. `position` or `absorption/3`; empty when there is no
entity or the pointer names the entity itself.

path.description: The validator's JSON pointer into the project.

Variant.description: A named set of material overrides on top of the base project.

overrides.description: At most one per group, strictly ascending by group id (so each variant has one spelling).

WebviewInfo.description: The webview engine and its runtime version, for the self-test and the Console.

version.description: `None` when the runtime cannot be queried (it is then missing or broken).
